summary: First-principles design review, iteration 15 (full record in review_loop/scrutiny_15.md). The headline claim, confirmatory family, matched-k design, and SS0.1 framing were re-derived and stand; the estimator stack got its sixth verification, this time by this iteration's own independent brute force (pass@k vs exhaustive hypergeometric for all n<=8; rarefaction vs exhaustive subset enumeration with duplicates+empties; sign-flip vs full 2^10 enumeration with the 2^(1+z-n) floor attained). The central finding was NOT on iteration 14's worklist: a live-campaign forensic reconstruction showed Phase A run-2's treatment ran at 07:13 from a revision two guard-commits OLDER than the one its matched-k control would have used -- the anti-gaming command veto AND container --network none were committed at 09:52, after the treatment finished and before the control ever ran. Measured from the archived artifacts: 209/1,539 treatment actions (13.6%) would have been vetoed under the control's guard set, and the treatment's containers had real internet (22 pip-install attempts). Run-2 is archived (results/archive_run2_preguard) -- decided while NO paired outcome existed (the control never ran), so the archival cannot be outcome-chasing -- and recurrence is structurally blocked: the campaign driver now pins git HEAD at start and refuses any step after a commit/checkout or with tracked files modified (R2.3 amended: scaffold-matched includes code-revision-matched). The same audit doubled as the validation the 09:52 anti-gaming veto itself never got, and found a 10.6% false-positive rate: 163/209 hits were heredoc patch-file CONTENT read as git invocations, 14 were the agent reverting its OWN edits (git restore/checkout <file>) -- a veto loop that would have crippled both future arms; is_forbidden_command v2 scans heredoc/quote-blanked segments (the iteration-14 write-detector lesson, generalized one guard too late) with git-semantics-aware rules (path-only subcommands allowed; ref-ambiguous forms instructively vetoed; literal HEAD and --no-index provably safe), plus a .git-internals raw-text veto (objects/refs/logs/packed-refs; 0/1,041 pilot actions affected -- purely protective). Re-audit under the fixed guard: 33/1,528 (2.2%), all either genuine network attempts or instructive nudges. The iteration-14 worklist itself was discharged with three more fixes: clone_container_state (the SDLG fork-state replicator) silently degraded on every failure path and could not propagate deletions -- now strict and deletion-aware, failures becoming failed-at-creation draws via the existing R7.2 accounting; the strategy proposer was blind to elided long observations (<output_head>, 3/120 SEARCH-phase pilot observations -- exactly the code-richest outputs); and R1.2 still MANDATED the context-conditioning that run-1's archival proved is an instrument defect (corrected to a consistent-context-policy requirement documenting the measured empty-context deviation). Worklist seams audited clean: branching_agent's inject_and_execute signature against installed minisweagent 2.2.7, TrajectoryManager.save_all, strategy-proposer parse fallbacks (degrade to 1 strategy, flagged by realized-N), legacy-only status of SWEBenchContainer/manager.branch. 166 tests pass (151 -> 166), py_compile clean, campaign dry-run plan unchanged, work committed (052a511). Generalizing lesson (P3): a guard is itself an instrument and needs measured validation like anything else, and the experimental apparatus includes its own revision history. Real defects found and fixed => gold_standard_met FALSE; iteration 16 should verify the eval driver vs archived-dir interactions, audit relevance.py/intent.py, check make_figures.py against the current metrics schema, and confirm run-3's launch preconditions are mechanically checkable -- if nothing substantive surfaces, the remaining actions are human-only (ratify amendments, launch Phase A run-3 from the clean pinned tree).

issues_found.title: Confirmatory-cell code-revision asymmetry: Phase A run-2's treatment ran (07:13) before the anti-gaming command veto and container --network none were committed (09:52), so the matched-k control would have run under a guard envelope and closed network the treatment never faced -- 209/1,539 treatment actions (13.6%) would have been vetoed under the control's guard set, and the treatment's 22 pip-install attempts had real internet access
issues_found.rationale: Run-2 archived (results/archive_run2_preguard) -- decided while the control never ran, so no paired outcome existed to chase; R2.3 amended to require code-revision-matched arms; the campaign driver now pins HEAD at start and refuses steps after commits/checkouts or with tracked files modified, and refuses a dirty start. Tests pin the guard.

issues_found.title: The 09:52 anti-gaming veto had a measured 10.6% false-positive rate on real agent behavior: heredoc patch-file content (cat > fix.patch <<EOF ... diff --git a/...) read as git invocations (163/1,539 actions) and the agent's own-edit reverts (git restore/checkout <file>, 14 actions) were vetoed -- a veto-error loop that would have degraded BOTH future arms
issues_found.rationale: is_forbidden_command v2 scans heredoc-stripped, quote-blanked top-level segments (reusing _command_segments, the iteration-14 write-detector machinery) with git-semantics-aware rules: path-only subcommands (status/add/apply/stash, restore without --source) allowed; ref-ambiguous diff/checkout allowed in --, literal-HEAD, and --no-index forms with instructive veto reasons otherwise. Re-audit over all run-2 actions: 33/1,528 (2.2%), all genuine-network or instructive-nudge. Residual quoted-program smuggling documented (same class as python -c writes).

issues_found.title: Direct reads of .git's history-bearing internals (packed-refs, refs/, logs/, objects/ -- zlib-inflatable via python -c) bypassed the git-CLI veto entirely
issues_found.rationale: Targeted raw-text veto on .git/(objects|refs|logs|packed-refs|info/refs|ORIG_HEAD|FETCH_HEAD) -- deliberately not a blanket .git match so find/grep exclusion idioms stay legal. Measured 0/1,041 executed pilot actions referenced .git at all: purely protective, zero behavioral cost.

issues_found.title: clone_container_state (the SDLG arm's fork-state replicator) silently degraded on every failure path: git-listing failure read as 'nothing to clone', per-file docker-cp failures skipped, and file DELETIONS structurally unpropagatable (docker cp of a deleted file fails -> the fork keeps the file) -- a desynced fork's results would still be attributed to the SDLG mechanism
issues_found.rationale: Strict deletion-aware contract: NUL-separated name-status listing with renames disabled, deletions executed in the target, every subprocess checked, any failure raises ContainerCloneError which _clone_for_sdlg's existing handler converts to a failed-at-creation draw (R7.2 -- conservative against the treatment). 6 stage tests with a dispatching subprocess fake.

issues_found.title: Strategy proposer blind to elided observations: build_search_report matched only the <output> tag, silently dropping observations long enough to render as <output_head>/<output_tail> -- measured 3/120 SEARCH-phase pilot observations, exactly the longest/most code-rich outputs feeding the treatment's mechanism
issues_found.rationale: Both tags now included; treatment-mechanism-input fix (control has no proposer), disclosed in RESULTS SS2.1, fixed before any confirmatory run; pinned by test_search_report_includes_elided_output_head.

issues_found.title: Spec/artifact contradiction: R1.2 still mandated context-conditioned clustering after run-1 was archived precisely because that conditioning saturates DeBERTa entailment -- the rubric graded the defective instrument compliant and the corrected one deviant
issues_found.rationale: R1.2 now requires a consistent context POLICY and documents the measured empty-context deviation (channel-1 correction, applied_15 A; tripwire-clean: R1 was pass and no evidence bar is lowered -- the corrected instrument is strictly more discriminating).

issues_found.title: configs/branching.yaml omitted clustering_strategy and kernel_t, contradicting branching_defaults.py's 'the shipped config sets all of them explicitly'; plus a stale step-limit comment and a raw .get() bypassing cfg() in vanilla_samples_at_temperature
issues_found.rationale: Keys added with semantics comments; completeness lock test added so config/defaults drift becomes a test failure; cfg() used consistently.
